articleTitle: Computer-aided determination of impedance matching domain
publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: In the analysis and design of impedance matching networks a very significant issue is how to determine their matchable domains. In this paper a simple but effective and general approach for the problem is given. A general-purpose programme of plotting the impedance matching domains is developed. The work may be of substantial interest to workers in various fields of electrical and electronic engineering.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: On the generation of differential-mode active filters
publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: The author describes circuit techniques to allow a wide range of single-ended circuits to be converted to differential form. A differential-mode circuit can be generated by converting the single-ended sections to symmetrical balanced two-ports. This method is presented by means of examples.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Instability trends in the fast Kalman and FTF algorithms
publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: The authors investigate the effects that the forgetting factor and the order of the filter have on the stability of the fast Kalman and fast transversal filters algorithms for adaptive system identification, and suggest reasons for the differences in behaviour of the two versions of the latter algorithm.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: Addresses the application of recursive filters in adaptive signal filtering. Simulations are performed, of the adaptive enhancement of sinusoidal signals embedded in white Gaussian noise, based on LMS algorithm. A digital version of Tellengen's theorem is used to evaluate the exact instantaneous gradient for parameter updates. The feasibility of implementing IIR-LMS filtering is being studied, and instability is found to be the major problem. The linear gradient approximation is shown to be a satisfactory method, offering stability and simplicity in computation. It is also decided that a second order recursive filter is the suitable form for this application.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A GaAs signal shaping network with a controlled response from DC to 25 GHz
publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: The authors describe how a GaAs monolithic microwave integrated circuit (MMIC) signal shaping network with a controlled response from DC to 25 GHz was designed, fabricated and tested. The network is a post-detection filter for use in a 15 Gbit/s optical fibre transmission system that uses narrow, soliton like pulses. They begin by outlining the design philosophy that defined the target response. This is followed by a brief description of the GaAs technology used to realise the filter. The impact of the parasitics associated with the technology are outlined which leads onto a description of the optimisation method adopted that includes the process parasitics inside the optimisation loop. Simulation results for the GaAs filter are given followed by measured data to illustrate the very tight control over the frequency response possible with MMIC realisations if care is taken during the design.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: An efficient hardware architecture implementing wave digital filters with reduced wordlength coefficients
publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: Discusses the design and implementation of a wave digital filter architecture using coefficients that are taken from a restricted range. It outlines the possible advantages of this approach, with comparison to traditional complete coefficient ranges. Estimates of hardware speed in a VLSI implementation are made with reference to the ES2 1.5-micron process.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Ladder based transconductor-capacitor filter and equaliser design
publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: Describes a topological matrix decomposition method for ladder based transconductor-C filter design and for an equally terminated ladder prototype filter this gives a realisation in which all the transconductance values are identical. Both conventional and low-impedance input transconductor sections can be utilised in filter and equaliser design. Fewer transconductors are required by the topological decomposition method than by the other ladder based transconductor-capacitor design techniques. The low sensitivity properties common to all the ladder based methods are preserved and comparative sensitivity studies including cascade biquad circuits are shown. The problem of realising such ladder based structures with a canonic number of transconductors is addressed.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Comparison of alternative approaches to digital deghosting of television pictures
publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: Compares the Texas Instruments TMS320 with the Analog Devices 210X DSP microcomputers in the specific application of deghosting television pictures. For reference purposes comparisons are made with the Intel 80X86 family of microprocessors.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: Two different approximation methods are considered in this paper-the bilinear transformation, and the all-pole approach. Each method has its advantages, but it will be seen that the all-pole design gives superior selectivity, for a given amount of calculations per input cycle. The bilinear transformation method takes advantage of analogue filter designs, which are mapped into the digital domain. The all-pole digital filters is based on a new mapping between the z plane and the w plane.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: The application of simulated annealing to multiple criterion optimisation design of IIR digital filters
publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: The problem addressed in this paper is that of designing IIR (infinite impulse response) digital filters to meet a frequency response specified in both magnitude and delay (or phase). The authors are concerned with the application of Multiple Criterion Optimisation (MCO) to IIR digital filter design. The Simulated Annealing optimisation method is introduced and it is shown how this technique may overcome some of the problems associated with MCO. As an example, the design of a fourth order band pass filter is considered.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Noise analysis for high-order active filters
publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: Generalised analysis of high-order continuous-time active filters removes previous restrictions and is confirmed by experiment. Particular attention is directed at multiple-loop structures.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: A RAM based architecture for the implementation of bit serial digital filters
publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: Bit-serial implementations of digital signal processing algorithms often find favour where reduced implementation area is an important design criterion since they facilitate an efficient trade-off between silicon area and data throughput. Area-wise the adoption of a bit-serial regime not only offers single wire communication paths, but also allows the use of one-bit arithmetic operators. This paper presents a methodology and architecture which will facilitate the adoption of standard RAM compiled cells for bit serial digital filtering. The paper presents the method and general architecture, and describes a design which has been realised using this technique based on the Xilinx 4000 series FPGA. Finally, complexity comparisons are made between the new and conventional approaches.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>

articleTitle: Evaluation of biquad and LC ladder implementations for switched capacitor filter designs
publicationTitle: IEE Twelfth Saraga Colloquium on Digital and Analogue Filters and Filtering Systems
abstract: The author evaluates what can be achieved using single ended biquad and LC ladder filter architectures. The performance parameters investigated are: frequency response sensitivity to capacitor variation; offset; power supply rejection; and noise. A seventh order low pass filter has been designed for the evaluation purpose. The design, measurements and simulation results are presented.<<ETX xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">></ETX>
